name: Interferon Regulatory Factor 8 Deficiency

criteria.description: Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the IRF8 gene
Severe reduction or absence of circulating dendritic cells and monocytes
Recurrent or severe infections with mycobacterial and viral pathogens
Abnormal immunophenotyping showing impaired myeloid lineage differentiation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of biallelic IRF8 pathogenic variants plus clinical evidence of dendritic cell and monocyte deficiency with recurrent mycobacterial or viral infections
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing combined with immunophenotyping and clinical presentation.

pathognomonic.notes: Marked reduction or absence of dendritic cells in peripheral blood
Infections with atypical mycobacteria or BCG vaccine strain

common.notes: Frequent infections with herpesviruses and respiratory viruses
Persistent fungal infections of skin and mucous membranes
Enlarged lymph nodes due to chronic infections
Poor growth in infancy and early childhood
Enlargement of liver and spleen secondary to infection or immune dysregulation

occasional.notes: Mild to moderate reduction in neutrophil count
Due to infections or immune dysregulation

rare.notes: Encephalitis or neuroinflammation secondary to infections

laboratory: Severe monocytopenia and dendritic cell deficiency on flow cytometry
Lymphopenia with normal or reduced neutrophils
imaging: Chest X-ray or CT showing granulomatous lesions or lymphadenopathy
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in IRF8 gene confirmed by sequencing
other: Impaired myeloid lineage differentiation on bone marrow biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: GATA2 mutations with broader hematopoietic defects
Presence of lymphedema and pulmonary alveolar proteinosis
Normal dendritic cell counts but impaired cytokine signaling

redFlags: Severe, recurrent infections with atypical mycobacteria
Marked monocytopenia and dendritic cell deficiency
Poor or adverse reactions to BCG vaccination
references: Hambleton S et al. IRF8 mutations and human dendritic cell immunodeficiency. N Engl J Med. 2011.
Salem S et al. Human IRF8 deficiency impairs dendritic cell development and function. J Clin Invest. 2014.
